standard.title: Justify production choices
standard.description: select, justify and use suitable materials, components, tools, equipment, skills and processes to safely make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can select and use suitable materials, components, tools, equipment and techniques to safely make designed solutions (AC9TDE6P03). They can select and use materials but have not yet justified selections with evidence, compared traditional and emerging technologies, or independently managed safety risks.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select, justify and use suitable materials, components, tools, equipment, skills and processes to safely make designed solutions, including comparing traditional and contemporary technologies and managing risks through safe, inclusive working practices.

nodes.label: Selecting materials and processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select suitable materials, components, tools, equipment and processes for a design task based on their properties and the design requirements
nodes.minimum_width: Select materials and processes for a design task; state why each is suitable based on at least one property or requirement
nodes.typical_width: Compare traditional, contemporary and emerging technology options for the same design task; select by weighing properties against requirements including sustainability and waste reduction
wider: Compare and evaluate alternative materials, components or techniques including emerging technologies to reduce waste or time
Investigate how the same design task would be approached differently using traditional vs contemporary materials and techniques
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who know only conventional materials cannot meaningfully compare alternatives at Node 2 — justification requires having encountered enough options to explain why the chosen one is most appropriate rather than simply available.
success_criteria: Selects materials and processes relevant to the design task
States why each selection is suitable based on a property or requirement

response_modes.reason: Material and process selection requires encountering a range of traditional, contemporary and emerging options before students can compare and choose. Students who only know conventional materials cannot evaluate emerging alternatives. Building the repertoire of available options is the prior condition for justified selection at Node 2.

nodes.label: Justifying selections
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can justify their material, tool and process selections by explaining why each choice is the most appropriate option for the design requirements
nodes.minimum_width: Justify at least one selection by comparing it against an alternative; explain why the chosen option better meets the requirements
nodes.typical_width: Justify selections across the design — materials, tools and processes — by referencing test results, properties, sustainability considerations and fitness for purpose; acknowledge trade-offs made
wider: Use online tutorials or digital tools to develop expertise with an unfamiliar technique, then justify why the new technique is more appropriate than a familiar one
Limited width — justification is the same analytical skill regardless of what is being justified. The breadth comes from the variety of materials and contexts, which is captured at Node 1.
success_criteria: Justifies at least one selection by comparing against an alternative
Explains why the chosen option better meets the design requirements

response_modes.reason: Justification is the command term shift from 5-6 ('select and use') to 7-8 ('select, justify and use'). Students who can select but not justify will make reasonable choices they cannot explain — which means they cannot improve their choices based on feedback or transfer their reasoning to new contexts. Seeing justification modelled across different types of selections (materials, tools, processes) helps build the habit.

nodes.label: Identifying production hazards and risks
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify material, equipment and process hazards relevant to their production task and plan safe working practices before production begins.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two production hazards relevant to the materials and equipment being used; plan a safe working practice for each before production starts.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and plan for hazards across the full production process — PPE, ventilation, equipment-specific hazards, material risks; establish inclusive working practices before starting production.
wider: Assess long-term health and environmental impacts of production choices — not just immediate safety risks.
Produce a safety information resource (e.g. checklist, guide) that details risks and safe practices for a specific production context.
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a risk identification and safe practice plan completed before production, Node 4 (safe and inclusive production) has no plan to follow — students who skip this step cannot respond to hazards appropriately because they have not anticipated them.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two risks relevant to the production task
Plans a safe working practice for each risk before production begins

response_modes.reason: Risk identification before production requires habitual practice — students need to develop the routine of checking hazards before starting. The skill doesn't vary conceptually across contexts but must become automatic.

nodes.label: Safe and inclusive production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply safe and inclusive working practices throughout production, managing hazards as they arise.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply planned safe working practices during production; identify and respond to at least one unexpected hazard that arises.
nodes.typical_width: Apply safe, independent, inclusive working practices consistently throughout production; practise techniques to improve expertise; manage workspace hazards as they arise.
wider: Reflect on how safe practice decisions affected production efficiency and quality — what would you change next time?
Limited width — safe production practice is a consistent habit. The breadth comes from the variety of production contexts, not from varying the practice.
success_criteria: Applies safe working practices consistently during production
Responds appropriately to at least one hazard that arises during production

response_modes.reason: Safe production practice requires habitual application — wearing PPE, managing workspace, responding to hazards. Repeated practice across production tasks builds the automatic habit.

nodes.label: Reflecting on safe practice after production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how safe working practices held up during production and identify improvements for future projects.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one safe practice decision after production — did it work as planned, and what would you change?
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on how risk identification and safe practice planning affected the production experience; identify specific safe practice improvements for a future project.
wider: Evaluate whether the production safety resource (if created at node 3) was accurate and useful — what would you update?
Reflect on how safe practice decisions affected production efficiency — were any safety measures unnecessarily restrictive or insufficiently protective?
success_criteria: Reflects on at least one safe practice decision after production
Identifies a specific improvement to safe practice planning for a future project

response_modes.reason: Reflecting on safe practice reinforces the habit of safety awareness — students who review what worked and what didn't build more robust safe practice habits for future projects.
